A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ULTRAIF. All 15 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison. Reorganized and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original instruction-following and general-capability experiments, training analyses, ablations, scaling results, and self-alignment experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds baseline results, Qwen2 experiments, sampling-efficiency measurements, contamination analysis, and human evaluation of filtering judgments.

M1.justification: Instruction decomposition, UltraComposer training, iterative augmentation, response filtering, SFT, iterative DPO, and final-iteration NCA remain unchanged. Training strategies move from v1 Section 2.4 to v2 Appendix A.3. The additional composer prompt documents the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v2 explicitly uses SPaR's released training data for its added 8k-data comparator (Appendix A.1.2 and Table 1); v1 only cites SPaR. ULTRAIF's ShareGPT, OpenHermes2.5, and No Robots sources and existing evaluation tasks remain unchanged. Qwen2 experiments reuse existing benchmarks.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds an evaluated SPaR baseline under GPT-4o-mini supervision, retaining the previous comparators. The new Qwen2 comparison in Table 6 includes Qwen2-7B-Instruct and AutoIF. SPaR's different supervisor and data budget limit direct comparisons with existing ULTRAIF settings.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen2-7B experiments, a human audit of 75 SFT examples with five annotators each, and contamination testing using 13-gram overlap and an LLM rephrasing detector. It also revises the reported scale-up SFT budget from 175k to 181k while retaining the scores; this does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test sampling pass rates across constraint counts and supervision settings (Table 4), filtering reliability against human judgments (Section 4.2), and training/test contamination (Table 5). Existing DPO, scaling, filtering, multi-turn, and case-study analyses remain, with several moved to Appendix C.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or a statistical testing procedure. v2 newly calls the unchanged LiveBench margin 'statistically significant' in Section 3.3, but supplies no supporting test or uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: v2 adds SPaR results, Qwen2 results, constraint-level pass rates, contamination ratios, and approximately 80% human-audit accuracy. Examples include SPaR's 54.71 IFEval Pr(S) in Table 1 and Qwen2 ULTRAIF+DPO's 45.28 in Table 6. Existing ULTRAIF scores in Tables 1–3 and retained plots are unchanged; the added backbone results are not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The decomposition, augmentation, SFT, DPO, and NCA equations are retained, including the losses relocated to Appendix A.3. Neither version contains additional theoretical proofs. v2's standard n-gram overlap formula documents an evaluation metric rather than introducing new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about scalable instruction synthesis, competitive instruction following, matching the LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct counterpart, and self-alignment. The conclusion's added mention of general benchmarks reiterates capabilities already claimed and evaluated in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds limitations concerning larger-model validation and LLM-supervision reliability, a distribution-fit explanation for smaller-supervisor benefits, and interpretations of the new reliability checks. Some wording overstates the evidence: Section 4.1 now describes iteration-three degradation on three benchmarks, although unchanged Table 3 shows IFEval improving.

D1.justification: v2 adds the UltraComposer input/output prompt template and explicit baseline reproduction sources in Appendices B and A.1.2. Code availability changes from a future promise to a statement that it is available. The Xtuner implementation disclosure is removed; hardware and optimization settings are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations supporting LLM judging, contamination detection, Qwen2, distribution fit, and preference-data filtering, including Zheng et al. (2023), Yang et al. (2023, 2024), Zhang et al. (2025), Li et al. (2025), and Si et al. (2025). The Xtuner citation disappears. The central positioning against existing instruction-synthesis approaches remains.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: training strategies move to Appendix A.3, existing efficiency and multi-turn analyses move to Appendix C, and appendices are regrouped into setup, prompts, and additional results. Method explanations, analysis paragraphs, and related work are condensed or rewritten. Limitations and acknowledgements replace the impact-statement section.

P2.justification: v2 changes typesetting throughout and converts the appendices to two columns. It adds three results tables and a composer prompt box, extends Table 1, and relocates and reformats retained displays. The self-alignment chart changes colors, legend terminology, and its vertical-axis minimum while preserving its results.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons, human filtering audit, contamination checks, reproducibility details, and explicit limitations make previously underexamined claims more assessable. These are useful but bounded gains: the human audit is sparsely documented, contamination conclusions exceed what nonzero overlap rates establish, and v2 introduces unsupported statistical-significance wording and a misleading interpretation of Table 3.
